decisions.reason: The black-finish range extends the existing drainage line at low cost and follows a clear design trend. It is only mentioned rather than featured, so its results are still uncertain, but the firm's established slack lets it carry the range through the evaluation period.

It has a page of its own and serves the growing demand for seamless floor coverings, which fits the firm's core competence. There is no sign of a shortfall that would trigger search for other uses of the resources.

Pump-assisted drainage is a more peripheral, niche technology and gets only a mention, which makes it the most likely candidate for a cut. Still, one year is too early to judge it against the aspiration level, and slack allows the firm to keep it for now.
The tileable floor drain is close to the firm's established product range and has its own page. That suggests results in line with aspirations, so there is little reason to drop it.
The stainless steel design grate builds on core metalworking capabilities and has its own page. It is a low-risk addition that management would retain.
